Points to Consider: The University of Rhode Island launched its Workday implementation on January 12, 2026, to replace its PeopleSoft Human Resources and Finance systems and the PBCS budgeting platform.
The project has successfully completed the Planning stage and is currently in the Architect and Configure stage, where functional and technical teams are configuring business requirements, validating system design, and testing configurations to ensure alignment with institutional needs.
Overall, the implementation remains on track across the majority of workstreams and continues to perform within planned timeline and budget expectations.

Project leadership and governance have remained stable and effective, providing consistent oversight and decision-making throughout the implementation.
State system integration remains the most significant project risk.
Identified early in the implementation, this dependency continues to present challenges because critical aspects of the integration effort are outside the direct control of URI and rely on State of Rhode Island stakeholders and timelines.
URI and the State of Rhode Island leadership team have been meeting monthly on the project status.
Change management continues to be a key factor for the implementation.
Over the past several weeks, outreach and engagement efforts have increased to provide opportunities for faculty, staff, and campus stakeholders to learn about the Workday program.
These activities are focused on building awareness, preparing the University community for upcoming changes, and driving adoption to support a successful transition to the new system .
Overall, the project remains on track , however we are mindful and maintain focus on risk management, stakeholder engagement, and organizational readiness.

Points to Consider: • The final appropriations bill includes a $4.2M increase to the General state Appropriation, with $1.3M intended for increased central costs. • The bill also includes $5M in operating dollars as startup funds for a Medical School. • The bill includes $15.2M in RICAP Asset Protection funds, $1.6M in new funding for Access Control, $9.0M (over 5 years) to address accessibility related projects, and $21M (over 5 years) to address building envelope projects. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: October 26, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of FY26 Financial Statements Purpose of Submittal: This is a request to recommend to the full Board of Trustees the approval of the University of Rhode Island's audited Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) Financial Statements.
Points to Consider: URI’s external auditors, CliftonLarsonAllen LLP, have completed their audit and have no audit findings.
The University will have a clean audit opinion for the year ending June 30, 2026.
Upon approval by the URI Board of Trustees, the FY 2026 financial statements will be issued.
Please refer to pp. 4-14 of the enclosed draft financial statements for the University’s Management's Discussion and Analysis, which provides a summary of our FY2026 statements.
A few highlights are outlined below. • The University reported an increase in net position of $88.48 million in FY26, up from $65.90 million in FY25.

This includes a $8.18 million decrease in net position before $96.66 million in capital contributions, which significantly contributed to the overall increase. • In FY26, operating revenues increased by $15.92 million (2.96%), compared to a $4.62 million (0.85%) decrease in FY25.
This decrease in FY25 was primarily due to a change in NACUBO reporting guidance that increased the scholarship allowance, which nets against tuition and fees. • Net tuition and fee revenue increased by $16.33 million due to an increase in tuition rates of 3.5% for both in-state students and out -of-state students and an increase in demand for housing, along with stronger retention rates.
Other operating revenues decreased slightly as the University outsourced the bookstore operations. • In FY26, operating expenses for the University increased by $21.93 million (3.2%), compared to a $25.30 million (3.8%) increase FY25.

The increase is comprised primarily of increases in salary and benefits, as well as other operating expenses such as utilities, repairs, and maintenance which have been impacted by broader economic factors. • When reviewing the University’s condensed statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net position, it is important to note that nonoperating revenue plays an important role in supporting the operations of the University.
The primary component of nonoperating revenues is State appropriations.
The State’s unrestricted appropriation represents the largest component of the University’s nonoperating revenues.
The University of Rhode Island is an equal opportunity employer committed to community, equity, and diversity.

• In FY26, the University received $117.04 million in State appropriations for operations, up from $112.74 million in FY25. While the State general appropriation did increase by 3.18% in FY26, the final general appropriation represented only 17% of URI’s overall request. The State’s general appropriation plays a critical role in supporting the University’s operating expenses, so the University continues to advocate for support of its full general appropriations request. The purpose of the MD&A is to assist readers in understanding the accompanying financial statements by providing an objective and understandable analysis of the University’s financial activities based on currently known facts, decisions, and conditions.
This analysis has been prepared by management, which is responsible for the completeness and fairness of the information contained therein.
The MD&A consists of highly summarized information, and it should be read in conjunction with the University’s financial statements and notes thereto that follow this section.
Overview of the Financial Statements The Universit y’s financial statements are prepared in accordance with GASB principles, focusing on the institution as a whole rather than on individual funds or activities.

The University reports its operations as a business -type activity, utilizing the economic measurement focus and the full accrual basis of accounting.
This approach allows the University to recognize revenues when earned and expenses when incurred, providing a comprehensive view of its financial performance.
As a component unit of the State of Rhode Island, the results of the University’s operations and net position are summarized in the State’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR).
This report is derived from the State’s government -wide financial statements, ensuring transparency and accountability in the University’s financial reporting within the broader context of state finances.
The University’s financial statements consist of three basic components that work together to provide a comprehensive picture of its financial health.
Each statement provides a different perspective: what the University owns and owes, how its financial position changed during the year, and how cash moved into and out of the University. 1.
Statement of Net Position: This statement provides a snapshot of the University’s financial position at the end of the fiscal year.

It reports the University’s assets and deferred outflows of resources, liabilities and deferred inflows of resources, and the resulting net position.
In simple terms, it helps readers understand the resources available to the University and its financial obligations.
Changes in net position over time can provide insight into whether the University’s overall financial position is strengthening or weakening. 2.
Statement of Revenues and Expenses and Changes in Net Position: This statement explains how and why the University’s net position changed during the fiscal year.
It reports revenues earned and expenses incurred during the year, regardless of when the related cash is received or paid.
For example, tuition revenue may be recognized when educational services are provided, even if payment is received later.
Similarly, expenses may be recognized before cash is paid, such as when employees earn leave benefits that will be paid in the future.
The resulting change in net position shows whether the University’s financial activities increased or decreased its net position during the year.

Statement of Cash Flows: While the statement of revenues and expenses reflects when revenues are earned and expenses are incurred, the statement of cash flows shows the actual movement of cash during the fiscal year.
Prepared using the direct method, it presents major categories of cash receipts and payments, including cash received from tuition and fees and cash paid to employees and suppliers.
This statement helps readers understand how the University generates and uses cash to meet its operating needs, invest in facilities and equipment, and meets its financing obligations.
How the Statements Work Together Taken tog ether, these three statements provide a more complete understanding of the University’s financial condition.
The statement of revenues and expenses explains the changes in net position during the year, while the statement of net position shows the cumulative financial results reflected in the University’s resources and obligations at year end.
The statement of cash flows adds another important perspective by showing whether and how those financial activities translated into cash receipts and payments.

Because revenues, expenses, and cash flows are measured differently, an increase in net po sition does not necessarily mean that the University’s cash balance increased.
Reviewing all three statements together helps readers better understand the University’s financial performance, resources, obligations, and ability to meet its financial needs.
